cities.name: Paris
cities.why: Every grand tour begins where the boulevards were invented. Three days of museums, markets and long café mornings set the tone before the rails carry you south.
must: Île de la Cité at dusk
food: Any proper boulangerie — eat it on a bench by the Seine
Classic bistro dinner; Le Relais de l'Entrecôte keeps it simple
Worth the queue at a pâtisserie in Saint-Germain
days: Musée d'Orsay early, Luxembourg Gardens picnic, browse Saint-Germain bookshops, golden-hour walk along the quays.
Sainte-Chapelle at opening, Île Saint-Louis ice cream, Marais passages and galleries, evening in a wine bar.
Covered-passage crawl, coffee at Rue des Martyrs, sunset from the Sacré-Cœur steps away from the crowds.
cities.transport: Métro carnet or Navigo Easy card; everything central is walkable
cities.stay: Le Marais or Saint-Germain for atmosphere within walking distance of both banks
tips: Book Sainte-Chapelle and Orsay timed entries ahead
Most museums close Monday or Tuesday — check before planning
Lunch prix-fixe menus are the affordable way into great kitchens

cities.name: Geneva
cities.why: The alpine hinge of the journey — a calm, watchmaker-precise city on a glacial lake, with the Alps standing by for a first proper mountain day.
gems: Perle du Lac park at sunset
food: Bains des Pâquis does a famously unfussy one on the pier
Geneva's own — old-town brasseries serve it with lentils
Small makers around Rue du Rhône beat the airport brands
days: Lake promenade to the Jet d'Eau, climb St Pierre's tower, wander the Old Town, swim or sauna at Bains des Pâquis.
Morning in Carouge's boutiques, afternoon boat across the lake or the Salève cable car for a first taste of altitude.
cities.transport: Free Geneva Transport Card from your accommodation covers trams, buses and lake boats
cities.stay: Pâquis for the lake and food stalls; Old Town for quiet cobbles
tips: Tap water everywhere is glacial and free — carry a bottle
Supermarket lunches (Migros, Coop) keep Swiss budgets sane
Sunday is genuinely quiet; plan the lake day for it

cities.name: Florence
cities.why: The Renaissance kept its capital small enough to walk. Three days lets you take the Uffizi slowly, climb the dome early, and still have an evening for the Oltrarno's workshops.
gems: Officina Profumo di Santa Maria Novella
food: Shared, rare, priced by the etto — trattorias in Sant'Ambrogio
From a street cart; the working Florentine's lunch
Look for covered tins and seasonal flavours, never neon mountains
days: Dome climb at opening slot, Baptistery mosaics, slow afternoon through Orsanmichele and the Bargello, aperitivo in Piazza della Signoria.
Uffizi until lunch, cross Ponte Vecchio to artisan workshops, Santo Spirito piazza for dinner.
Morning market at Sant'Ambrogio, walk up to San Miniato via Piazzale Michelangelo, sunset over the whole city.
cities.transport: Entirely walkable; the C-line electric minibuses help tired feet
cities.stay: Oltrarno for craft-shop mornings and quieter nights; Santa Croce for trattorias
tips: Dome and Uffizi tickets sell out days ahead — book both online
Cover charges (coperto) are normal, not a scam
Churches enforce covered shoulders; carry a light scarf

cities.name: Rome
cities.why: The destination every grand tour bent toward. Antiquity, baroque theatre and the best carbonara of your life, layered in one walkable, chaotic, golden city.
gems: Basilica di San Clemente's underground layers
food: Trastevere and Testaccio classics — no cream, ever
Fried rice croquettes; the pre-dinner street snack
Cream-filled brioche breakfast beloved by Romans
days: Colosseum first entry, Forum and Palatine until lunch, Aventine keyhole and orange-garden sunset, dinner in Testaccio.
Pantheon at opening, Piazza Navona and the Caravaggios of San Luigi, Trevi late evening when the crowds thin.
Vatican Museums early slot, St Peter's dome if legs allow, cross the river for a slow Trastevere night.
cities.transport: Walk the centre; metro B for the Colosseum, trams to Trastevere
cities.stay: Monti for boutiques near the ruins; Trastevere for the evenings
tips: Book Colosseum and Vatican slots well ahead — queues are brutal
House wine and water come cheap; order both
Drink from the nasoni street fountains — the water is excellent

cities.name: Venice
cities.why: The traditional finale — a city that still feels like a reward. Two nights means you keep the lagoon after the day-trippers leave and see it wake in the mist.
must: Grand Canal by vaporetto at night
food: Bar-hop bacari around Rialto with an ombra of wine
Select or Cynar, standing by a canal, before dinner
days: Basilica at opening, Doge's Palace secret itineraries, get lost toward Castello, night vaporetto down the Grand Canal.
Dawn photos while streets are empty, Cannaregio bacari crawl, San Giorgio tower for the final view of the whole tour.
cities.transport: 48-hour vaporetto pass pays for itself; otherwise walk everything
cities.stay: Cannaregio or Castello — real neighbourhoods ten minutes from the crush
tips: Day-trip crowds peak 10–16h; do icons outside that window
A tide app warns you about acqua alta in autumn
Sit-down coffee in Piazza San Marco costs a fortune — stand at the bar
